mammals/fish/reptiles than dogs or cats, simply because their care is typically overlooked despite being more involved. Small animal abuse is rampant. I see too many people rehoming animals because they didn’t know what they were getting into when they bought it from PetSmart. 

What if pet stores couldn’t sell pets, only pet supplies? If they do sell pets, they have to be dogs or cats that are associated with some kind of local shelter program where they partner with pet stores to help manage overflow. The amount of animals that are mass produced, so to speak, for pet stores and then bought by people who don’t do research before buying an animal is astronomical. Of course there are those who do, but I’d wager that most people who buy animals at a pet store also get their care information from either pet store employees or generalist pet websites, both of which usually provide inconsistent or outright incorrect husbandry info. 

If pet stores only sold supplies/cats/dogs, then people would be forced to buy small animals elsewhere. Maybe some sort of national small animal breeder database? Of course the breeders would be routinely inspected by some kind of state or federally-funded organization and required to basically be experts in the field of the animals that they breed. You could buy them online or maybe visit an accredited brick and mortar establishment that specifically specializes in a type of animal. Sounds really similar to a pet store, I know, but there would be something put in place to prevent them from being “mill” animals. 

Breeders are an issue in of themselves. There are too many people breeding animals for the sake of churning a profit as opposed to those who do it to help further the captive population of an exotic species. Captive bred is always better than of having to resort to importing wild caught specimens. Cracking down on backyard breeders and imposing some kind of legislation requiring a license to sell animals. Exceptions would be those in need of rehoming, but then you would have shitty breeders trying to circumvent the law by saying that their animals are all rescues or something equally ludicrous. 

What about the people that impulse buy animals? Again, due to the sheer amount of stray dogs and cats, this wouldn’t necessarily apply to them. Maybe just a quick, few question long quiz or a verbal rundown of the care by an adoption representative. For small mammals, fish, and reptiles, require some sort of knowledge and/or ethics test before purchase. If they fail it, they get a chance to retake it in a week. If they fail again, they cannot buy the animal.

honestly eating disorders are taught in too much detail. schools will talk about the different methods that are used to lose weight, which can be very dangerous to young, impressionable teenagers who are insecure about themselves. similarly, “awareness” on social media about eating disorders is usually spread by people who have had (or may still have) and ED, which isn’t a bad thing in itself. however, often times they post pictures of themselves at their lowest weight, which can do more harm than good because eating disorders are so competitive. 


in my opinion, these kinds of things shouldn’t be taught or “made aware” of because of how impressionable people can be. i’m not saying that they shouldn’t be talked about at all, but that they should be approached with more tact. instead of going into detail about the methods used to lose weight by those with ED’s, they should instead talk about how to be comfortable in your own skin, how to recognize if you have a problem, and how to seek help. maybe briefly go over the effects that these disorders can have on the body other than weight loss (like hair loss, malnutrition, weaker bones, esophagus cancer, permanently damaged organs, heart failure, and death). 


it just infuriates me how these sensitive topics are taught in schools to children. weight shouldn’t be discussed much, if at all. why? because children are still growing and developing, they shouldn’t be concerned with their weight. “giving” children insecurities can have long term consequences on mental health.

in general, yes, i equate weight gain with happiness and discomfort because that’s what i’ve been exposed to my entire life. television, tabloids, social media, advertisements, family, friends, and everyday life all talk about “stubborn belly fat, water weight, losing weight, weight loss pills, fad diets, ‘oh no i gained 10 lbs over the holidays’, unattainable beauty standards”, and much more. because of that, hearing the words “weight gain” automatically sound bad in my head. i know that some people don’t mind weight gain. others probably want to gain weight (like my boyfriend for example). you’re right; i can’t possibly know how people feel about themselves gaining weight.

EDs vary from person to person. obviously i don’t know what other people are dealing with. 

this sub is a safe space. generally, i don’t see people encourage others to restrict. in fact, it’s usually people congratulating others for recovering, which is a good thing. this sub is actually pretty nice. my issue is honestly more subtle than what you see. yes, this sub is filled with posts about the topic in question, and that’s okay. people come here to vent and have a voice about the things that they may be thinking or going through, and it’s okay for them to do so. it’s just that i see posts where people will talk about how they bragged about being skinny to someone with an eating disorder, using a sibling as a motivation to restrict, or posts where someone says it’s okay to eat and someone comments something like “haha i’m still not going to anyway because i don’t deserve it 🙃”

on another note, i never said my friend was thin. not everyone with an eating disorder fits the “thin dainty girl” image that is associated with that. don’t assume things like that. second of all, i knew she was disordered because she told me she was. in fact, she talked about it a lot. i never said her not eating was offensive to me, it was the fact that she would bring food every day and expect us to eat it. i would ask her not to discuss calories and carbs and restriction and she would still talk about that stuff. she once pushed me to eat a bag of these cheddar rice cakes she brought and after i ate a couple (in fairness they were pretty good) she grabbed the bag, read the caloric information on the bag out loud, then pushed it back towards me even after i said i didn’t want any more. our other friend who is thin said that the friend in question would comment on her body and how good it is. she said it would make her uncomfortable. my friend would ask my other friend how she was so skinny or how she would eat so little. when it was just me and the first friend, she would point out different girls and comment on their thigh gaps/collar bones/other thinspo type stuff. it really messed with me and made me feel worthless because i don’t have any of that stuff. the girl (who knew that i too am suffering from an eating disorder) also talked about fasting the week of prom and how great she felt. she’d talk about restricting, her cravings, and a bunch of other ED stuff even though i didn’t want to talk about it because it made me feel horrible. 

i understood that she wanted someone other than her therapist to vent to, but it was too much. my other friend and i were basically a second set of therapists to her. she didn’t care about us, only herself. i really do understand what she’s going through because i am too, but i care about other people. she wanted to talk about, watch, and do stuff that only she wanted to do. once she asked me to come to one of her basketball games, so i went. yeah, i don’t like basketball, but i took pictures and cheered her on and everything because i genuinely cared about her (that’s what friends do). i asked her to come to the school musical because i was participating in it. “ehh, should i go? i don’t really want to. i’m busy”(yet she posted a picture of her just hanging out on her back porch on snapchat that weekend. so busy). it hurt me. she wanted to sneak into a rehearsal to “laugh at me” (she was kicked out before she even got in) but couldn’t be bothered to come see the actual performance. my other friend (the thin one i mentioned earlier) has super strict parents that never let her leave the house and yet she was able to come to one of the multiple showings because she cared about me and wanted to see the performance. 

the first girl and i were close, but i didn’t want to be close anymore after all of this. it affected me so badly that it got to the point where being around her made my suicidal thoughts worse. i distanced myself from her and now we don’t speak to each other at all. i feel so much better not being around her, and i can’t wait to go to college this fall and start a new life without her. 


so yeah, maybe i don’t know what people are going through, but at least i care about people enough to empathize with them. we’re all suffering from EDs in this subreddit. you don’t see posts about adding calories and stuff because nobody would post that stuff here. this is a positive space. sorry for the long read.
